key_insight: Nearly uniform upward liquid flow from clean spherical bubble chains is explained by the spatial superposition of each bubble’s far wake, which depends on the actual bubble trajectories rather than just dispersion width.
engineering_relevance: This enables a reduced-order predictor for bubble-induced liquid flow in multiphase equipment, useful for designing and interpreting bubbly flows in reactors, columns, and other fluid systems.
method: High-accuracy embedded-boundary simulations of aligned clean spherical bubble chains
Resolved interfacial boundary layers and long-range bubble–bubble hydrodynamic interactions
Built a reduced-order far-wake superposition model and tested it on measured bubble trajectories
evidence_signal: The model reproduced the experimentally observed nearly uniform upward liquid flow, while a uniformly dispersed bubble arrangement with the same dispersion width did not.
watch_item: The reduced-order model depends on accurate bubble trajectory information and may be less reliable if wake interactions or bubble shapes deviate from the clean spherical-chain regime.
paper_title: Prediction of Spherical Bubble-Chain-Induced Liquid Flow through Far-Wake Superposition Based on Bubble-Chain Hydrodynamics
